26.en: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

26.zh: 于是，王和巡抚并百妮基与同坐的人都起来，
26.en: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

26.zh: 退到里面，彼此谈论说：「这人并没有犯什么该死该绑的罪。」
26.en: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”

26.zh: 亚基帕又对非斯都说：「这人若没有上告于凯撒，就可以释放了。」
26.en: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

27.zh: [非斯都]既然定规了，叫我们坐船往意大利去，便将保罗和别的囚犯交给御营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。
27.en: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

27.zh: 有一只亚大米田的船，要沿着亚细亚一带地方的海边走，我们就上了那船开行；有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古和我们同去。
27.en: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.

27.zh: 第二天，到了西顿；犹流宽待保罗，准他往朋友那里去，受他们的照应。
27.en: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

27.zh: 从那里又开船，因为风不顺，就贴着塞浦路斯背风岸行去。
27.en: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

27.zh: 过了基利家、旁非利亚前面的海，就到了吕家的每拉。
27.en: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

27.zh: 在那里，百夫长遇见一只亚历山大的船，要往意大利去，便叫我们上了那船。
27.en: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

27.zh: 一连多日，船行得慢，仅仅来到革尼土的对面。因为被风拦阻，就贴着克里特背风岸，从撒摩尼对面行过。
27.en: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

27.zh: 我们沿岸行走，仅仅来到一个地方，名叫佳澳；离那里不远，有拉西亚城。
27.en: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

27.zh: 走的日子多了，已经过了禁食的节期，行船又危险，保罗就劝众人说：
27.en: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them

27.zh: 「众位，我看这次行船，不但货物和船要受损伤，大遭破坏，连我们的性命也难保。」
27.en: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

27.zh: 但百夫长信从掌船的和船主，不信从保罗所说的。
27.en: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

27.zh: 且因在这海口过冬不便，船上的人就多半说，不如开船离开这地方，或者能到菲尼基过冬。菲尼基是克里特的一个海口，一面朝东北，一面朝东南。
27.en: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.

27.zh: 这时，微微起了南风，他们以为得意，就起了锚，贴近克里特行去。
27.en: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

27.zh: 不多几时，狂风从岛上扑下来；那风名叫「友拉革罗」。
27.en: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

27.zh: 船被风抓住，敌不住风，我们就任风刮去。
27.en: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.

27.zh: 贴着一个小岛的背风岸奔行，那岛名叫高大，在那里仅仅收住了小船。
27.en: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

27.zh: 既然把小船拉上来，就用缆索捆绑船底，又恐怕在赛耳底沙滩上搁了浅，就落下篷来，任船飘去。
27.en: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

27.zh: 我们被风浪逼得甚急，第二天众人就把[货物]抛在海里。
27.en: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

27.zh: 到第三天，他们又亲手把船上的器具抛弃了。
27.en: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

27.zh: 太阳和星辰多日不显露，又有狂风大浪催逼，我们得救的指望就都绝了。
27.en: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

27.zh: 众人多日没有吃什么，保罗就出来站在他们中间，说：「众位，你们本该听我的话，不离开克里特，免得遭这样的伤损破坏。
27.en: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.

27.zh: 现在我还劝你们放心，你们的性命一个也不失丧，惟独失丧这船。
27.en: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

27.zh: 因我所属所事奉的　神，他的使者昨夜站在我旁边，说：
27.en: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

27.zh: 『保罗，不要害怕，你必定站在凯撒面前，并且与你同船的人，　神都赐给你了。』
27.en: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

27.zh: 所以众位可以放心，我信　神他怎样对我说，事情也要怎样成就。
27.en: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

27.zh: 只是我们必要撞在一个岛上。」
27.en: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

27.zh: 到了第十四天夜间，船在亚得里亚海飘来飘去。约到半夜，水手以为渐近旱地，
27.en: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

27.zh: 就探深浅，探得有十二丈；稍往前行，又探深浅，探得有九丈。
27.en: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

27.zh: 恐怕撞在石头上，就从船尾抛下四个锚，盼望天亮。
27.en: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

27.zh: 水手想要逃出船去，把小船放在海里，假作要从船头抛锚的样子。
27.en: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

27.zh: 保罗对百夫长和兵丁说：「这些人若不等在船上，你们必不能得救。」
27.en: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

27.zh: 于是兵丁砍断小船的绳子，由它飘去。
27.en: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.

27.zh: 天渐亮的时候，保罗劝众人都吃饭，说：「你们悬望忍饿不吃什么，已经十四天了。
27.en: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

27.zh: 所以我劝你们吃饭，这是关乎你们救命的事；因为你们各人连一根头发也不至于损坏。」
27.en: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

27.zh: 保罗说了这话，就拿着饼，在众人面前祝谢了　神，擘开吃。
27.en: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.

27.zh: 于是他们都放下心，也就吃了。
27.en: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

27.zh: 我们在船上的共有二百七十六个人。
27.en: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

27.zh: 他们吃饱了，就把船上的麦子抛在海里，为要叫船轻一点。
27.en: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

27.zh: 到了天亮，他们不认识那地方，但见一个海湾，有岸可登，就商议能把船拢进去不能。
27.en: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

27.zh: 于是砍断缆索，弃锚在海里；同时也松开舵绳，拉起头篷，顺着风向岸行去。
27.en: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

27.zh: 但遇着两水夹流的地方，就把船搁了浅；船头胶住不动，船尾被浪的猛力冲坏。
27.en: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

27.zh: 兵丁的意思要把囚犯杀了，恐怕有洑水脱逃的。
27.en: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

27.zh: 但百夫长要救保罗，不准他们任意而行，就吩咐会洑水的，跳下水去先上岸；
27.en: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

27.zh: 其余的人可以用板子或船上的零碎东西上岸。这样，众人都得了救，上了岸。
27.en: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.

28.zh: 我们既已得救，才知道那岛名叫马耳他。
28.en: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

28.zh: 土人看待我们，有非常的情分；因为当时下雨，天气又冷，就生火接待我们众人。
28.en: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.

28.zh: 那时，保罗拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一条毒蛇，因为热了出来，咬住他的手。
28.en: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.

28.zh: 土人看见那毒蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说：「这人必是个凶手，虽然从海里救上来，天理还不容他活着。」
28.en: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”

28.zh: 保罗竟把那毒蛇甩在火里，并没有受伤。
28.en: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.

28.zh: 土人想他必要肿起来，或是忽然仆倒死了；看了多时，见他无害，就转念，说：「他是个神。」
28.en: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.

28.zh: 离那地方不远，有田产是岛长部百流的；他接纳我们，尽情款待三日。
28.en: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.

28.zh: 当时，部百流的父亲患热病和痢疾躺着。保罗进去，[为他]祷告，按手在他身上，治好了他。
28.en: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

28.zh: 从此，岛上其余的病人也来，得了医治。
28.en: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.

28.zh: 他们又多方地尊敬我们；到了开船的时候，也把我们所需用的送到船上。
28.en: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

28.zh: 过了三个月，我们上了亚历山大的船往前行；这船以「宙斯双子」为记，是在那海岛过了冬的。
28.en: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”

28.zh: 到了叙拉古，我们停泊三日；
28.en: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

28.zh: 又从那里绕行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天就来到部丢利。
28.en: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

28.zh: 在那里遇见弟兄们，请我们与他们同住了七天。这样，我们来到罗马。
28.en: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

28.zh: 那里的弟兄们一听见我们的信息就出来，到亚比乌市和三馆地方迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢　神，放心壮胆。
28.en: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

28.zh: 进了罗马城，保罗蒙准和一个看守他的兵另住在一处。
28.en: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

28.zh: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们来了，就对他们说：「弟兄们，我虽没有做什么事干犯本国的百姓和我们祖宗的规条，却被锁绑，从耶路撒冷解在罗马人的手里。
28.en: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

28.zh: 他们审问了我，就愿意释放我；因为在我身上，并没有该死的罪。
28.en: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

28.zh: 无奈犹太人不服，我不得已，只好上告于凯撒，并非有什么事要控告我本国的百姓。
28.en: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

28.zh: 因此，我请你们来见面说话，我原为以色列人所指望的，被这链子捆锁。」
28.en: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”

28.zh: 他们说：「我们并没有接着从犹太来论你的信，也没有弟兄到这里来报给我们说你有什么不好处。
28.en: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

28.zh: 但我们愿意听你的意见如何；因为这教门，我们晓得是到处被毁谤的。」
28.en: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

28.zh: 他们和保罗约定了日子，就有许多人到他的寓处来。保罗从早到晚，对他们讲论这事，证明　神国[的道]，引摩西的律法和先知的书，以耶稣的事劝勉他们。
28.en: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.

28.zh: 他所说的话，有信的，有不信的。
28.en: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

28.zh: 他们彼此不合，就散了；未散以先，保罗说了一句话，说：「圣灵借先知以赛亚向你们祖宗所说的话是不错的。
28.en: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

28.zh: 他说： 你去告诉这百姓说： 你们听是要听见，却不明白； 看是要看见，却不晓得；
28.en: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.

28.zh: 因为这百姓油蒙了心， 耳朵发沉， 眼睛闭着； 恐怕眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白，回转过来， 我就医治他们。
28.en: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, then I would heal them.’

28.zh: 所以你们当知道，　神这救恩，如今传给外邦人，他们也必听受。」
28.en: “Be it known therefore to you that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”
When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

28.zh: 保罗在自己所租的房子里住了足足两年。凡来见他的人，他全都接待，
28.en: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house and received all who were coming to him,

28.zh: 放胆传讲　神国[的道]，将主耶稣基督的事教导人，并没有人禁止。
28.en: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
